_meta.title: Named dimensions — what loom already computes, and what the meaning layer will need
_meta.status: RECORD ONLY. Nothing reads this file. It exists so candidate dimensions are captured as they arise rather than reconstructed later.
_meta.timeline: Exploring the ideas: autumn 2026. Initial build: the LLM class, spring 2027. Do not start building before then.
why: The maintainer's target is an n-dimensional INTERPRETABLE graph. What separates that from an embedding is that the dimensions have NAMES, so two things can be near each other AND you can say why.

The prompting case: 'black out', 'go unconscious' and 'taking an unintended short nap' mean nearly the same thing and must cluster — but they share almost no STRUCTURE. loom analyses them as three different verbs with three different argument shapes, so decomposition alone will never connect them.

The observation that shapes this file: loom ALREADY produces named discrete dimensions. Ten of them, listed below. The interpretable-dimension architecture is not the missing piece — the SEMANTIC axes are.
_meta.the_connecting_rule: COMPOSITIONAL MEANS COMPUTABLE; NON-COMPOSITIONAL MEANS IT NEEDS A STATED EDGE. 'go out' is derivable from 'go' plus 'out' and needs no edge in the graph. 'black out' needs one — for exactly the same reason it must be taught as a phrase-level heart word. One fact decides both the lesson and the data structure.

computed._note: Already produced by loom today, from the letters and the structure. Named values, not coordinates. These are free — any meaning layer starts with them rather than re-deriving them.

dimensions.name: verb_evidence
dimensions.note: How loom knows this is a verb. A confidence CLAIM, not a score.
dimensions.no_established_term: No standard feature corresponds. UD, GF and FrameNet all describe what a structure IS, not how confident the analyser is that it got there — so the evidence grades and Certain/Ambiguous attachment are loom-specific and have nothing to interoperate with.

dimensions.name: split_evidence
dimensions.note: How loom knows this word has parts.
dimensions.no_established_term: No standard feature corresponds. UD, GF and FrameNet all describe what a structure IS, not how confident the analyser is that it got there — so the evidence grades and Certain/Ambiguous attachment are loom-specific and have nothing to interoperate with.

dimensions.name: attachment
dimensions.note: Whether a modifier's target is in doubt — ambiguity as a first-class value.
dimensions.no_established_term: No standard feature corresponds. UD, GF and FrameNet all describe what a structure IS, not how confident the analyser is that it got there — so the evidence grades and Certain/Ambiguous attachment are loom-specific and have nothing to interoperate with.

dimensions.name: rank
dimensions.note: What KIND of unit this is, when the caller does not know in advance.
dimensions.also_called: GF RGL: S / NP — the sentence-versus-noun-phrase split GF makes with its own categories

computed._interoperability: FIVE OF THE TEN map almost exactly onto Universal Dependencies features, down to the value names: UD writes Polarity=Pos|Neg, Tense=Past|Pres|Fut, Aspect=Perf|Prog, Voice=Act|Pass, Number=Sing|Plur. That alignment was not designed in — both arrived at the same categories because they are the traditional ones — and it means loom's grammatical dimensions can be exchanged with the UD ecosystem without a translation layer. Recorded as an interoperability KEY only: category names are not copyrightable, and no UD or GF code or data is used here. Same discipline as base-verbs.json, which records the GF RGL category beside each frame (transitive=V2, ditransitive=V3, clausal=VS).

proposed._note: Semantic axes. NONE of these is derivable today. Recorded as candidates with the case that produced them, so the spring work starts from evidence rather than from a blank page.
proposed._expect: The honest version will be authored the way `frames` was — a small teachable set, attested against a corpus, grown. Nothing automates the step from a dictionary's 'to lose consciousness' to a feature [-conscious]; FrameNet, Wierzbicka's semantic primes and Jackendoff's conceptual structure all stayed hand-built.

dimensions.name: change_of_state
dimensions.question: Does the subject end up different from how it started?
dimensions.also_called: Vendler telicity; Dowty proto-PATIENT entailment "undergoes change of state"

dimensions.name: consciousness
dimensions.question: Is awareness gained or lost?
dimensions.note: Narrow. May turn out to be one value of a broader faculty axis.

dimensions.name: duration
dimensions.question: Brief or extended?
dimensions.also_called: Vendler durativity — the punctual/durative split behind achievements vs accomplishments

worked_example._note: The cluster that prompted the whole idea. They land NEAR each other and not identically — and the difference is sayable, which is the entire point.

proposed._terminology_finding:
THREE OF THE FOUR are already named in the literature, with the same content: change_of_state is Vendler telicity and Dowty's proto-patient entailment; volition is Dowty's proto-agent "volitional involvement"; duration is Vendler durativity. Adopting those names costs nothing and connects the work to fifty years of argument about exactly these distinctions.

THE FOURTH, consciousness, HAS NO ESTABLISHED TERM — and that is a signal rather than a gap. The other three are FEATURES OF AN EVENT: is it bounded, is it chosen, is it instantaneous. consciousness is not; it is what the event is ABOUT. Mixing the two grains into one axis set is probably a category error, and the likely resolution is that event features and semantic FIELD are different kinds of dimension that both belong in the graph, on different axes. Worth settling before the spring build rather than during it.

buildable_now._note: Separate from the research problem, and worth keeping separate. This produces EDGES with evidence; it does not produce named dimensions.
buildable_now.method: Definition overlap (the Lesk method). Two expressions link when their Webster 1913 `Defn:` lines share content words, and the shared words ARE the evidence — 'these cluster because both definitions say consciousness'. No overlap, no claim.
buildable_now.source: Webster's Unabridged Dictionary 1913, Project Gutenberg #29765, public domain. Already fetched; see vocabulary-measurement-system/data/PROVENANCE.md.
buildable_now.alternative: WordNet synsets are this relation pre-built, at the cost of attribution licensing rather than public domain.
